text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: realtime-infer-prod queue depth > 95th pct for 3m, latency SLO breach starting. Pager: cheng (oncall)
cheng (oncall): I'm on it. seeing elevated enqueue times and a handful of 5xx from runtime.
ops-bot: Pager duty triggered: high-queue-depth -> paging cheng. Incident link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2234
cheng (oncall): Initial triage: queue spiking on model-pool-gpu-a, HPA target pods not increasing. Could be warmup bottleneck.
tara (infra): copying logs, checking HPA events and GPU pool allocation now. If HPA didn't scale, maybe metrics pipeline lagged.
maria (runtime): adding runtime traces. I see many new sessions with kv-cache miss + cold-start latency of ~700ms per request at the model front.
james (sre): Any customer-facing errors? Are clients seeing 5xx or just slow responses?
cheng (oncall): Early look: about ~12% 5xx spike, mostly 503/504 from the inference proxy when pool is saturated. SDK timeouts observed.
sam (eng): tagging relevant owners for model warmup: @maria @tara - could warmup queue/sidecar be stuck?
maria (runtime): past 10s logs:
```
WARN warmup: failed warmup attempt for shard=3, err=timeout
INFO warmup: enqueued warmup job for model-id=redwood/text-xxl, trace=tx-9a3
ERROR kv-cache: miss for prefix, warming triggered
```
cheng (oncall): HPA status (from cluster):
```
kubectl get hpa -n prod model-pool-gpu-a
NAME                 REFERENCE                TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS   AGE
model-pool-gpu-a     Deployment/model-pool-a   75%/80%    2         12        2          4h
```
cheng (oncall): HPA shows targets at 75/80% and replicas stuck at 2. No scaling events in last 5m.
tara (infra): Checking metrics pipeline (prometheus -> hpa adapter). Adapter logs show last scrape delayed ~2m. Might explain late scaling.
ops-bot: infra-alert: k8s-metrics-server latency increased in eu-west1 for ~3m.
james (sre): If HPA adapter lagged, we should manually scale to relieve pressure. Recommend scale to 6 pods as a quick mitigation.
maria (runtime): Manual scale will help, but warmup still needed per pod. We should also trigger async warmup-burst to prefill kv-cache.
sam (eng): Can we patch runtime to accept temporary lower batch sizing to let requests through while warmup finishes?
cheng (oncall): Immediate actions: 1) manual scale model-pool-gpu-a to 6 2) trigger warmup-burst for model redwood/text-xxl 3) increase request timeout for proxy to reduce 5xx churn. I'll run changes and update.
cheng (oncall): Running: `kubectl scale deploy model-pool-a --replicas=6 -n prod`
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Scale command executed by cheng. pods launching...
maria (runtime): Triggering warmup-burst: `POST /internal/warmup?model=redwood/text-xxl&mode=burst` -> accepted.
(Logs streamed)
maria (runtime): Warmup progress: started 4 warmup workers per pod. kv-cache fill rate improving.
cheng (oncall): Proxy timeout tweak: bump to 30s for the route to prevent upstream 504s while scaling/warmup finishes.
ops-bot: route-config: proxy timeout updated by cheng, rolling config push succeeded.
james (sre): Monitoring: queue depth falling from 980 -> 420 in the last 2m. 5xx rate down to +4% over baseline. Still some customer latency.
tara (infra): Metrics pipeline recovered around +2m ago. HPA adapter now reporting fresh metrics. Should observe autoscale behavior returning to normal.
sam (eng): Hypothesis checklist (start thread RCA here):
- H1: metrics-adapter latency caused delayed HPA scale -> pool starved -> queue backpressure and increased cold-starts
- H2: warmup worker concurrency lower than expected on pod startup -> per-pod warmup slower than expected
- H3: KV-cache eviction thrash (new traffic pattern) causing repeated cold paths
- H4: HPA config target/threshold mismatch for sudden traffic bursts

maria (runtime): Adding logs to thread for timeline building:
```
# t0 - 2234566990 - traffic burst begins, queue climbs from 80->600
# t0+90s - 2234567080 - metrics adapter shows scrape delay of ~120s
# t0+150s - 2234567140 - HPA didn't scale (replicas=2), queue near 900
# t0+210s - 2234567200 - manual scale to 6 triggered, warmup request started
# t0+300s - 2234567290 - queue down to 400, 5xx rate dropping
```
cheng (oncall): Customer impact note: Several API customers saw timeouts for short window (~3-4 minutes). Support notified; we'll collect request IDs and correlate.
james (sre): I pulled sample traces; majority of 5xx are upstream proxy returning 503 when worker pool not available. Saving traces to the incident doc.
tara (infra): Config checks: HPA configured to scale on custom metric `inflight_tokens_per_pod` with threshold 80%. Adapter scrapes `pod_inflight` from prometheus. We'll verify scrape frequency and adapter timeouts.
sam (eng): Runtime note: default warmup per pod starts 1 worker per GPU; maybe insufficient for large models. I propose a deferred change: warmup concurrency = min(4, gpus_per_pod) for hot models. Will open PR.
maria (runtime): For RCA, I'm attaching snippets of warmup logs and kv-cache stats to the incident doc. Preliminary verdict: warmup throughput was main limiter; adapter lag was enabler for H1.
cheng (oncall): Hands-off period: I'll remain until clear, then hand off to james in 30m for post-incident follow-up. Please update this thread with any new hypotheses or logs.
james (sre): Taking handoff at 2234567600. I'll own RCA coordination and support follow-up with customer comms. Starting checklist for RCA: timeline, metrics (hpa events, adapter latencies), warmup logs, kv-cache histogram, config diff of HPA and runtime.
sam (eng): Quick mitigation follow-ups we should track: (a) accelerate adapter scrape frequency in eu regions (b) increase warmup concurrency for heavy models (c) add transient scale override on autoscaler when adapter latency > X
maria (runtime): Agreed. Also propose an automatic warmup-burst trigger when queue depth per pool > 200 and replicas < desired.
tara (infra): I'll open infra task to harden metrics adapter and add alerts for adapter scrape anomalies.
james (sre): Noting action items into INC-2234-RT: TAGS: warmup, hpa-adapter, metrics, kv-cache, customer-impact.
cheng (oncall): Thanks all. Adding final note: incident severity reduced; continuing RCA in this thread. :thumbsup:
